question: What happens when beings see the Lord's many-limbed form?
premises: The great form has many mouths, eyes, arms, thighs, feet, bellies, tusks, and fangs
Worlds are agitated upon seeing it
inference: The terrifying multiplicity of the form disturbs all observers
uncertainties: pravyathitāstathā'ham fuses plural participle with first-person statement
plain_english: Seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, mighty-armed, with many arms, thighs, feet, bellies, tusks, and fangs, the worlds are agitated, and so am I.
